components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house or shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 完; a hand 寸 under a roof means guarding.
寸 (hand, inch) — originally a hand, as in 对, 寻, 封.

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá shǒu zài ménkǒu.
example.english: The police are standing guard at the door.
example.fact: 守 is to guard and to keep a promise or a rule: 守信, 守时 (to be punctual), 守规矩. 守岁 is the New Year's Eve custom of staying up late to welcome the new year.

examples.hanzi: 我们守在电话旁边。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shǒu zài diànhuà pángbiān.
examples.english: We stayed by the phone.

examples.hanzi: 他是个守信用的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè shǒu xìnyòng de rén.
examples.english: He is a man who keeps his word.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and attitudes: 想, 思, 感; 态 is one's attitude.
太 (tài) sounds exactly like 态.
广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.

example.hanzi: 他对工作的态度非常认真。
example.pinyin: Tā duì gōngzuò de tàidù fēicháng rènzhēn.
example.english: His attitude toward work is extremely serious.
example.fact: 态度 almost always appears with the preposition 对 marking what the attitude is directed at ("对 + X + 的态度," "attitude toward X") — dropping 对 and simply placing the target noun before 态度 is a common structural slip for learners translating directly from English "attitude toward."

examples.hanzi: 她对客人的态度很热情。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì kèrén de tàidu hěn rèqíng.
examples.english: Her attitude toward guests is very warm.

examples.hanzi: 你这是什么态度?我在跟你好好说话。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhè shì shénme tàidu? Wǒ zài gēn nǐ hǎohāo shuōhuà.
examples.english: What's with that attitude? I'm talking to you nicely.

components.note: 尢 (lame leg) — 尢 is a bent, limping leg, as in 尤, 就; 尴 describes an unsteady, awkward position.
监 (jiān) — near sound — 尴 is gān; 监 also sounds out 篮 lán.
尢 (lame leg) — 尢 is a limping leg, as in 尤, 就; 尬 is awkwardness, and appears almost only in 尴尬.
介 (jiè) — loose hint — 尬 is gà; 介 also sounds out 界 jiè.

example.hanzi: 他在会议上说错了名字,场面很尴尬。
example.pinyin: Tā zài huìyì shàng shuō cuò le míngzi, chǎngmiàn hěn gāngà.
example.english: He got the name wrong at the meeting, and the scene was very awkward.
example.fact: 尴尬 is one of a small class of Mandarin words where neither character carries an independent meaning outside the pair — both 尴 and 尬 exist mainly to spell the sound of this one word for social awkwardness, and both happen to share the 尢 radical (a bent, lame leg), fittingly evoking an unsteady, off-balance feeling.

examples.hanzi: 她忘了他的名字,觉得很尴尬。
examples.pinyin: Tā wàng le tā de míngzi, juéde hěn gāngà.
examples.english: She forgot his name and felt very awkward.

examples.hanzi: 大家都不说话,气氛有点儿尴尬。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu bù shuōhuà, qìfēn yǒudiǎnr gāngà.
examples.english: Everyone was silent and the atmosphere was a bit awkward.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言, as in 说, 话, 请; 诺 is a spoken promise.
若 (ruò) — near sound — 诺 is nuò; 若 also sounds out 惹 rě.

example.pinyin: Tā shì ge yí nuò qiān jīn de rén.
example.english: He is a man whose word is his bond.
example.fact: 诺 is a bound form for promising: 承诺 (to commit), 诺言 (a promise), 一诺千金 (one promise worth a thousand gold). It also writes the first syllable of 诺贝尔 (Nobel).

examples.hanzi: 他向我承诺，不会反悔。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng wǒ chéngnuò, bú huì fǎnhuǐ.
examples.english: He promised me and won't go back on it.

examples.hanzi: 他是个重承诺的人，说到做到。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè zhòng chéngnuò de rén, shuōdào zuòdào.
examples.english: He takes promises seriously and does what he says.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people, as in 他 he, 们 plural, 住 live; 你 is "you".
尔 (ěr) is a loose sound clue for nǐ; 尔 also supplies 您 nín (polite you, with 心 added).
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.pinyin: Nǐhǎo, hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ.
example.english: Hello, nice to meet you.
example.fact: 你好 literally means "you [are] good" — a plain subject-plus-adjective sentence repurposed as a fixed greeting formula, much like English "how do you do" long ago stopped being a real question and became a set phrase.

examples.hanzi: 你好,请问这里有人吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, qǐngwèn zhèlǐ yǒu rén ma?
examples.english: Hello, is anyone sitting here?

examples.hanzi: 他笑着对我说:“你好!”
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàozhe duì wǒ shuō: "Nǐ hǎo!"
examples.english: He smiled and said hello to me.

components.note: 隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.
人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.

example.hanzi: 这件事的结果难以预料。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì de jiéguǒ nányǐ yùliào.
example.english: The outcome of this matter is hard to predict.
example.fact: 难以 only ever attaches directly before a following verb (难以想象 "hard to imagine," 难以忘记 "hard to forget") and can't stand alone the way its plainer synonym 难 can (很难, "very difficult") — a narrower, more literary register reserved for formal or written Mandarin.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事让人难以相信。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi ràng rén nányǐ xiāngxìn.
examples.english: This story is hard to believe.

examples.hanzi: 我难以决定该选哪一个。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ nányǐ juédìng gāi xuǎn nǎ yí ge.
examples.english: I find it hard to decide which one to choose.

components.note: 木 (tree) — two trees side by side make a grove or forest; compare 森 with three.

example.pinyin: Zhè piàn shùlín hěn dà.
example.english: This forest is very large.
example.fact: 林 is two 木 for a wood, and three 木 make 森 (sēn, dense forest). It is also one of the most common Chinese surnames (Lín), and 林 can mean any circle of people, as in 艺林 (art circles).

examples.hanzi: 森林里有很多树。
examples.pinyin: Sēnlín lǐ yǒu hěn duō shù.
examples.english: There are many trees in the forest.

examples.hanzi: 他姓林，是我的同学。
examples.pinyin: Tā xìng Lín, shì wǒ de tóngxué.
examples.english: His surname is Lin, and he is my classmate.

components.note: 又 (hand) — a hand holding a branch 十: to prop up, support; 支 also sounds out 枝 zhī branch and 肢 zhī limb.
票 (ticket) — originally flames flying up, which is why 票 gives the sound piào/piāo to 漂 and 飘 and biāo to 标; ticket is a later meaning.

example.hanzi: 他开了一张支票付房租。
example.pinyin: Tā kāi le yì zhāng zhīpiào fù fángzū.
example.english: He wrote a check to pay the rent.
example.fact: 票 (built from 覀, once a picture of rising flames, over 示, "altar") originally named the paper burned in ritual offerings, and later broadened to any officially printed paper of value — the same root behind 票 in 车票 ("ticket"), 选票 ("ballot"), and 支票 ("check"), all different kinds of significant paper.

examples.hanzi: 这张支票的有效期是三个月。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhīpiào de yǒuxiàoqī shì sān ge yuè.
examples.english: This check is valid for three months.

examples.hanzi: 你能收支票吗?我身上没带现金。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng shōu zhīpiào ma? Wǒ shēn shang méi dài xiànjīn.
examples.english: Do you accept checks? I don't have any cash on me.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 拼 is to put together.
并 (bìng) hints at the sound: 拼 pīn is close to 瓶 píng, which shares it.

example.hanzi: 我们把两张桌子拼在一起。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen bǎ liǎng zhāng zhuōzi pīn zài yìqǐ.
example.english: We pushed the two tables together.
example.fact: 拼 is to join pieces: 拼图 (jigsaw puzzle), 拼音 (Pinyin, literally "spell the sounds"), and 拼车 (to carpool). It also means to give it everything: 拼命 (to go all out), 拼搏 (to struggle hard).

examples.hanzi: 孩子在拼一个很大的拼图。
examples.pinyin: Háizi zài pīn yí gè hěn dà de pīntú.
examples.english: The child is putting together a big puzzle.

examples.hanzi: 他拼命努力，想考上好大学。
examples.pinyin: Tā pīnmìng nǔlì, xiǎng kǎo shàng hǎo dàxué.
examples.english: He works with all his might to get into a good university.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球, 现, 理: 玩 first meant to handle jade.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.

example.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì zhēn hǎowán.
example.english: This game is really fun.
example.fact: 好玩 literally combines 好 ("good") with 玩 ("to play") into "good to play with" — describing an activity or thing as entertaining, distinct from 有趣 ("interesting"), which can describe an idea or person with no element of play involved at all.

examples.hanzi: 这个公园很好玩,我们明天再来吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gōngyuán hěn hǎowán, wǒmen míngtiān zài lái ba.
examples.english: This park is fun, so let's come again tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 这本书一点儿也不好玩。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yìdiǎnr yě bù hǎowán.
examples.english: This book isn't fun at all.

components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 时, 晚, 明: the sun at the top of a sprout, early morning. 早 also gives 草 cǎo and 澡 zǎo.
食 (food) — eating and meals: 饭, 饿, 饱 (as 饣); 餐 is a meal.

example.hanzi: 我每天早上七点吃早餐。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn chī zǎocān.
example.english: I eat breakfast at seven o'clock every morning.
example.fact: 早餐 is the more formal, written-register word for "breakfast" alongside the more colloquial 早饭 — both pair 早 ("early, morning") with a word for "meal" (餐 vs. 饭), the same pattern that produces 午餐/午饭 ("lunch") and 晚餐/晚饭 ("dinner").

examples.hanzi: 早餐你想吃面包还是鸡蛋?
examples.pinyin: Zǎocān nǐ xiǎng chī miànbāo háishi jīdàn?
examples.english: Would you like bread or eggs for breakfast?

examples.hanzi: 酒店的早餐从七点开始。
examples.pinyin: Jiǔdiàn de zǎocān cóng qī diǎn kāishǐ.
examples.english: The hotel's breakfast starts at seven.

components.note: 艹 (grass, 草字头) — marks plants and herbs, as in 花 flower, 草 grass, 菜 vegetable; 茶 is tea, from a plant; 人 and 木 below show a tree-like tea bush.

example.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng hē chá háishi hē kāfēi?
example.english: Would you like tea or coffee?
example.fact: Languages borrowed the word for tea from two Chinese sources: "chai" and "cha" trace back to Mandarin or Cantonese chá, while English "tea" comes from Min Chinese te via Dutch traders. In China 茶 can also mean tea-like infusions, such as 花茶 and 奶茶.

examples.hanzi: 我们喝茶吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen hē chá ba.
examples.english: Let's have tea.

examples.hanzi: 这种茶叶很香。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng cháyè hěn xiāng.
examples.english: This kind of tea leaf smells lovely.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech and sound, as in 吃, 唱, 问: 唯 first meant a quick reply, yes.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) is a close sound clue for wéi; 隹 also in 维 wéi and 惟 wéi.

example.pinyin: Wéiyī de bànfǎ jiùshì děng.
example.english: The only way is to wait.
example.fact: 唯 is a bound form in written Chinese: 唯一 (the only), 唯有 (only), 唯独 (solely). It is pronounced exactly like 维 and 惟 (also wéi), which is why 惟一 is sometimes seen as a variant of 唯一.

examples.hanzi: 唯一的问题是时间不够。
examples.pinyin: Wéiyī de wèntí shì shíjiān bú gòu.
examples.english: The only problem is that there isn't enough time.

examples.hanzi: 这家店唯有周日不开门。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn wéi yǒu zhōurì bù kāimén.
examples.english: This shop is closed only on Sundays.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.

example.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà shí zǒngshì hěn zìxìn.
example.english: She always speaks with confidence.
example.fact: 自信 combines 自 ("self") with 信 ("to believe, to trust") into a transparent "to believe in oneself" — the same 信 root that appears in 相信 ("to believe/trust something") and 信任 ("trust"), all sharing the core idea of placing faith in something.

examples.hanzi: 要对自己有自信,你一定行。
examples.pinyin: Yào duì zìjǐ yǒu zìxìn, nǐ yídìng xíng.
examples.english: Have confidence in yourself, you can definitely do it.

examples.hanzi: 他上台演讲时很自信。
examples.pinyin: Tā shàng tái yǎnjiǎng shí hěn zìxìn.
examples.english: He was confident when giving his speech on stage.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.

example.pinyin: Wǒ mèimei míngnián kāishǐ shàngxué.
example.english: My younger sister starts school next year.
example.fact: 上学 uses 上 in its verb sense "to go to, to attend" rather than its more familiar meaning "on top of" — the same pattern behind 上班 ("to go to work") and 上课 ("to attend class"), where 上 marks heading to a regular, recurring activity or place.

examples.hanzi: 孩子六岁就要上学了。
examples.pinyin: Háizi liù suì jiù yào shàngxué le.
examples.english: A child starts school at the age of six.

examples.hanzi: 今天我要早点起床上学。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒ yào zǎodiǎn qǐchuáng shàngxué.
examples.english: Today I need to get up early to go to school.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地 earth, 坐 sit; 在 is "to be at a place".
才 (cái) is a close sound clue for zài; 才 also appears in 材 cái.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shū fàngzài zhuōzi shàng.
example.english: Please put the book on the table.
example.fact: 放在 pairs 放 ("to release, to put down") with 在 ("at, in") to specify exactly where something ends up — it almost always appears inside a 把-construction ("把 + object + 放在 + location," as here), one of the standard templates Mandarin uses to mark where an acted-upon object is moved to.

examples.hanzi: 他把钥匙放在了口袋里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ yàoshi fàng zài le kǒudài lǐ.
examples.english: He put the keys in his pocket.

examples.hanzi: 我不知道眼镜放在哪里了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhīdào yǎnjìng fàng zài nǎlǐ le.
examples.english: I don't know where I put my glasses.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.hanzi: 海洋里有很多奇特的生物。
example.pinyin: Hǎiyáng lǐ yǒu hěn duō qítè de shēngwù.
example.english: There are many strange creatures in the ocean.
example.fact: 生物 combines 生 ("life, to be born") with 物 ("thing, object") into a literal "living thing" — the same 生 root also appears in 生命 ("life") and 学生 ("student," literally close to "one born into learning"), each drawing on 生's core image of a shoot pushing up out of the ground.

examples.hanzi: 我哥哥在大学学生物。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge zài dàxué xué shēngwù.
examples.english: My older brother studies biology at university.

examples.hanzi: 这种生物只生活在深海里。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng shēngwù zhǐ shēnghuó zài shēnhǎi lǐ.
examples.english: This creature lives only in the deep sea.

components.note: 王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and discussion: 说, 议, 谈; 论 is debate and theory.
仑 (lún) gives the sound; same part in 轮 lún and 伦 lún.

example.hanzi: 这只是一个理论,还没有被证实。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì yí gè lǐlùn, hái méiyǒu bèi zhèngshí.
example.english: This is just a theory, it hasn't been proven yet.
example.fact: 理's 王 component is a truncated 玉 ("jade"), and the character originally described the natural grain running through a piece of jade — a concrete image of an underlying pattern that extended over time into "reason, logic, principle," giving 理论 its sense of an orderly underlying structure.

examples.hanzi: 这个理论听起来很有道理。
examples.pinyin: Zhège lǐlùn tīng qǐlái hěn yǒu dàolǐ.
examples.english: This theory sounds very reasonable.

examples.hanzi: 理论和实际常常不一样。
examples.pinyin: Lǐlùn hé shíjì chángcháng bù yíyàng.
examples.english: Theory and practice are often different.

components.note: 角 (horn, corner) — a picture of an animal horn. Read jiǎo for horn, corner and angle; jué for a role, as in 角色.
广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.

example.hanzi: 从这个角度看,这幅画更漂亮。
example.pinyin: Cóng zhège jiǎodù kàn, zhè fú huà gèng piàoliang.
example.english: Looking from this angle, the painting is more beautiful.
example.fact: 角度 extends its literal geometric sense ("angle," measured in 度, "degrees") into a common figurative one, "point of view" (从...角度看, "looking from the ... angle") — one of several spatial words in Mandarin, alongside 方面 ("aspect, side"), that double as ways to talk about how someone frames an argument.

examples.hanzi: 你要换个角度来想这个问题。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào huàn ge jiǎodù lái xiǎng zhège wèntí.
examples.english: You should look at this problem from a different angle.

examples.hanzi: 他站在一个很好的角度拍了照片。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhàn zài yí ge hěn hǎo de jiǎodù pāi le zhàopiàn.
examples.english: He took the photo from a great angle.

components.note: 年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.
纟 (silk, thread) — 纟 is the simplified 糸 (thread), as in 红, 给; 纪 first meant the thread end, then keeping record, as in 世纪.
己 (jǐ) — same sound, different tone — 纪 is jì; 己 also sounds out 记 jì.

example.hanzi: 他年纪不大,但是很有经验。
example.pinyin: Tā niánjì bú dà, dànshì hěn yǒu jīngyàn.
example.english: He's not old, but he's very experienced.
example.fact: 年纪 names a person's age and is used almost exclusively for people, while its near-synonym 年龄 is the more neutral, official-register word that also shows up in formal documents and statistics — similar to how English favors "how old are you" in speech but "age" on a form.

examples.hanzi: 你多大年纪了?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ duō dà niánjì le?
examples.english: How old are you?

examples.hanzi: 她年纪大了,走路要小心。
examples.pinyin: Tā niánjì dà le, zǒulù yào xiǎoxīn.
examples.english: She's getting on in years and needs to walk carefully.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the main part and radical, as in 张 and 引. Story: two arrows (丨丨) pulled across a bow, hence 'not, negative'; now mainly in foreign names like 弗兰克.
兰 (orchid) — simplified from 蘭, which had the grass radical 艹 on top and 闌 giving the sound lán — a plant name.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.

example.hanzi: 弗兰克是我的美国朋友。
example.pinyin: Fúlánkè shì wǒ de Měiguó péngyou.
example.english: Frank is my American friend.
example.fact: 弗兰克 transliterates the English name "Frank" purely by sound — 弗, 兰, and 克 each just supply a syllable (fú-lán-kè) with no connection to their literal meanings ("not," "orchid," "to overcome"), the standard way Mandarin renders foreign personal names with no ready-made Chinese equivalent.

examples.hanzi: 弗兰克今天要来我们家吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Fúlánkè jīntiān yào lái wǒmen jiā chīfàn.
examples.english: Frank is coming to our house for dinner today.

examples.hanzi: 弗兰克会说一点儿中文。
examples.pinyin: Fúlánkè huì shuō yìdiǎnr Zhōngwén.
examples.english: Frank can speak a little Chinese.

components.note: 车 (cart, simplified 車) — vehicles and transport: 转 turn, 输 transport, 较 compare; 轻 was a light cart.
The right half is a short form of 巠 (jīng), the sound part in 经 jīng, 径 jìng and 茎 jīng — a loose clue for qīng.

example.pinyin: Tā qīngqīng de guān shàng le mén.
example.english: She closed the door gently.
example.fact: 轻 means light in weight (the opposite of 重) and gentle in action: 轻轻地. It also gives 轻松 (relaxed, at ease), 年轻 (young) and 轻视 (to look down on).

examples.hanzi: 这个箱子很轻，我拿得动。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāngzi hěn qīng, wǒ nádedòng.
examples.english: This box is light; I can carry it.

examples.hanzi: 他年轻，没有经验。
examples.pinyin: Tā niánqīng, méiyǒu jīngyàn.
examples.english: He is young and has no experience.

components.note: 见 (see) — seeing and vision: 看, 现, 视, 览; 观 is to watch. 又 only stands in for the old sound part 雚 (guàn).
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: to look carefully inside.
祭 (jì) is a loose sound clue for chá; 祭 also sounds out 际 jì and 擦 cā.

example.hanzi: 科学家仔细观察了这只昆虫的行为。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā zǐxì guānchá le zhè zhī kūnchóng de xíngwéi.
example.english: The scientist carefully observed the insect's behavior.
example.fact: 观察 combines two verbs that both independently mean "to look, to watch" — 观 (as in 观看, "to view") and 察 (as in 察觉, "to detect, perceive") — into a single word for sustained, careful watching, distinct from a brief glance.

examples.hanzi: 医生需要观察病人几天。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng xūyào guānchá bìngrén jǐ tiān.
examples.english: The doctor needs to observe the patient for a few days.

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢观察天上的星星。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan guānchá tiān shang de xīngxing.
examples.english: He likes to observe the stars in the sky.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
鼠 (rat) — a picture of a rat with its teeth (臼 on top) and a tail; as a radical it is in rodent names.

example.pinyin: Chúfáng lǐ yǒu yì zhī lǎoshǔ.
example.english: There's a mouse in the kitchen.
example.fact: The 老 in 老鼠 isn't literally "old" — here it works as a fossilized, near-meaningless prefix that attaches to certain animal and kinship nouns for a familiar, colloquial ring (also seen in 老虎, "tiger," and 老师, "teacher"), rather than describing the mouse's actual age.

examples.hanzi: 猫在抓老鼠。
examples.pinyin: Māo zài zhuā lǎoshǔ.
examples.english: The cat is catching a mouse.

examples.hanzi: 这只小老鼠很怕人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī xiǎo lǎoshǔ hěn pà rén.
examples.english: This little mouse is afraid of people.

components.note: 九 — originally a bent arm (elbow), later borrowed to write nine. 九 also sounds out 究 jiū and 鸠 jiū.

example.pinyin: Xiànzài shì zǎoshang jiǔ diǎn.
example.english: It is nine in the morning.
example.fact: 九 sounds like 久 (jiǔ, long-lasting), which makes it auspicious, and as the largest single digit it stood for the emperor in 九五之尊. The Double Ninth Festival (重阳节) falls on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month.

examples.hanzi: 今天我们九个人去看电影。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒmen jiǔ gè rén qù kàn diànyǐng.
examples.english: Nine of us are going to the movie today.

examples.hanzi: 他九月开始上大学。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiǔyuè kāishǐ shàng dàxué.
examples.english: He starts university in September.

components.note: 凵 (open box) — the bottom part and dictionary radical. 击 simplifies 擊, whose 手 (hand) hinted at striking. Memory aid: a blow landing in a hollow.

example.hanzi: 足球队在比赛中击败了对手。
example.pinyin: Zúqiúduì zài bǐsài zhōng jībài le duìshǒu.
example.english: The football team beat its opponent in the match.
example.fact: 击 is mostly a bound form: 攻击 (to attack), 打击 (a blow, a setback), 射击 (to shoot), 击败 (to defeat). 点击 (to click) is the everyday computer verb.

examples.hanzi: 他在比赛中击中了球。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng jīzhòng le qiú.
examples.english: He hit the ball in the match.

examples.hanzi: 请敲门，不要大力撞击。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng qiāo mén, búyào dàlì zhuàngjī.
examples.english: Please knock; don't slam against the door.

components.note: 龙 — a picture of a dragon, simplified from 龍. It also sounds out 聋 lóng, 笼 lóng and 拢 lǒng.

example.pinyin: Lóng shì Zhōngguó wénhuà de xiàngzhēng.
example.english: The dragon is a symbol of Chinese culture.
example.fact: Chinese 龙 are not fire-breathing monsters: they are benevolent water and rain spirits and an imperial emblem. 龙年 is the Year of the Dragon, and 望子成龙 means to hope one's son will become a dragon, i.e. a success.

examples.hanzi: 中国人叫自己是龙的传人。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguórén jiào zìjǐ shì lóng de chuánrén.
examples.english: Chinese people call themselves descendants of the dragon.

examples.hanzi: 这条龙是用纸做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lóng shì yòng zhǐ zuòde.
examples.english: This dragon is made of paper.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks things to do with ground and soil, as in 地 ground, 坏 broken; 埋 is putting something into the earth.
里 (lǐ) — only a loose sound hint for mái today; mostly useful as the part that completes the shape.

example.pinyin: Gǒu bǎ gǔtou mái zài dìxià.
example.english: The dog buried the bone underground.
example.fact: 埋 is mái when it means to bury (埋头 "to bury one's head", to be absorbed in work) but mán in 埋怨 (to complain). The same verb is used for burying both objects and feelings: 埋藏.

examples.hanzi: 他把秘密埋在心里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ mìmì mái zài xīn lǐ.
examples.english: He buried his secret deep in his heart.

examples.hanzi: 他一直埋头工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìzhí máitóu gōngzuò.
examples.english: He kept his head down working.

components.note: 田 (field) — a field above 力 (strength): a man is one who works the fields with strength.
又 (hand) — two hands 又 stacked: hands joined in friendship.

example.pinyin: Tā dài nányǒu huí jiā jiàn fùmǔ.
example.english: She brought her boyfriend home to meet her parents.
example.fact: 男友 is a clipped, modern shorthand for the fuller 男朋友 ("boyfriend") — dropping 朋 much like English speakers sometimes shorten "boyfriend" to "bf" in texting, though 男友 is common enough in writing and speech to not read as especially casual.

examples.hanzi: 我男友下个月要来看我。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ nányǒu xià ge yuè yào lái kàn wǒ.
examples.english: My boyfriend is coming to see me next month.

examples.hanzi: 她的男友在一家银行工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā de nányǒu zài yì jiā yínháng gōngzuò.
examples.english: Her boyfriend works at a bank.

components.note: 关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.
扌 (hand) — hand radical for actions — 掉 is to drop or lose hold.

example.pinyin: Shuìjiào qián jìde guāndiào diànshì.
example.english: Remember to turn off the TV before going to bed.
example.fact: 掉 attached after a verb often marks that something is removed or eliminated as a result — 关掉 ("switch off," literally "close away"), 扔掉 ("throw away"), 忘掉 ("forget," literally "forget away") — a common verb-complement pattern for actions that make something disappear or cease.

examples.hanzi: 出门的时候请关掉所有的灯。
examples.pinyin: Chūmén de shíhou qǐng guāndiào suǒyǒu de dēng.
examples.english: Please turn off all the lights when you leave.

examples.hanzi: 你能把音乐关掉吗?我想睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng bǎ yīnyuè guāndiào ma? Wǒ xiǎng shuìjiào.
examples.english: Can you turn off the music? I want to sleep.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — eating and speech: 喝, 吸, 吗; 吃 is to eat.
乞 (qǐ) is only a loose sound clue for chī.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 惊 is a startled heart.
京 (jīng) sounds exactly like 惊; also in 鲸 jīng and 景 jǐng.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息,大家都很吃惊。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, dàjiā dōu hěn chījīng.
example.english: Hearing this news, everyone was very shocked.
example.fact: 吃惊 literally reads "to eat a shock" — 吃 here isn't about food but uses its broader sense of "to take in, to undergo" (also seen in 吃苦, "to endure hardship," literally "to eat bitterness"), a small family of idioms where 吃 marks experiencing something sudden or unpleasant rather than consuming it.

examples.hanzi: 她吃惊地看着我,说不出话来。
examples.pinyin: Tā chījīng de kàn zhe wǒ, shuō bù chū huà lái.
examples.english: She looked at me in shock, speechless.

examples.hanzi: 这么多人来了,我真的很吃惊。
examples.pinyin: Zhème duō rén lái le, wǒ zhēn de hěn chījīng.
examples.english: I'm really surprised that so many people came.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — marks vessels, as in 盘, 盒, 盆; 盖 is a lid, a cover over a vessel.

example.pinyin: Qǐng gài shang gàizi.
example.english: Please put the lid on.
example.fact: 盖 covers things in several ways: a lid (盖子), to put on a cover (盖被子, pull up the quilt), to stamp (盖章), and in everyday speech to build a house: 盖房子. Related words are 锅盖 (pot lid) and 盖饭 (rice with a topping).

examples.hanzi: 请把锅盖盖好。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ guōgài gàihǎo.
examples.english: Please cover the pot with its lid.

examples.hanzi: 他们在山边盖了一间小房子。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài shān biān gài le yì jiān xiǎo fángzi.
examples.english: They built a small house at the foot of the mountain.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
木 (wood) — 木 is wood and trees, as in 树, 板, 桌; buildings with floors were built of wood, hence 楼.
娄 (lóu) — same sound — 楼 is lóu; 娄 also sounds out 搂 lǒu.

example.pinyin: Zhè zuò dàlóu yǒu sānshí céng.
example.english: This building has thirty floors.
example.fact: 楼 alone already names a multistory building or a single floor within one (二楼, "the second floor") — 大楼 simply adds 大 ("big") to specify a sizeable one, typically an office or apartment tower, as distinct from a small standalone house (房子).

examples.hanzi: 我们公司在这座大楼的十五层。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī zài zhè zuò dàlóu de shíwǔ céng.
examples.english: Our company is on the fifteenth floor of this building.

examples.hanzi: 大楼里有电梯,不用爬楼梯。
examples.pinyin: Dàlóu lǐ yǒu diàntī, bú yòng pá lóutī.
examples.english: There's an elevator in the building, so there's no need to climb stairs.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 移 first meant grain swaying, then shifting and moving.
多 (duō) — the original sound clue — today 移 yí is only loosely related to 多 duō.
力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào yídòng zhè zhāng zhuōzi.
example.english: Please don't move this table.
example.fact: 移动 has picked up a specialized modern sense as an adjective, "mobile" (移动电话, "mobile/cell phone"; 中国移动, "China Mobile," a major carrier) — an old, generic verb for physical movement of any kind repurposed to describe untethered, portable technology.

examples.hanzi: 请把车往前移动一下。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ chē wǎng qián yídòng yíxià.
examples.english: Please move the car forward a little.

examples.hanzi: 我的手机一直在移动,地图上能看到。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī yìzhí zài yídòng, dìtú shang néng kàndào.
examples.english: My phone keeps moving, and I can see it on the map.

components.note: 冏 (bright/window) — the lower part; dictionary treats it as the 'bright' hint. Meaning 'trade, business' is better remembered as a market (商店).
口 (mouth) — dictionary radical, as in 吃 eat. Memory aid: a shop-keeper's mouth calling out prices; 商量 is to 'talk it over'.
广 (building, shelter) — houses and shops: 床, 库, 座; 店 is a shop.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound hint; same part in 站 zhàn and 战 zhàn.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn zhōumò bù yíngyè.
example.english: This store isn't open on weekends.
example.fact: 商 alone already means "commerce, trade" (as in 商人, "merchant," and 商业, "business"), and 店 names the physical premises (as in 饭店, "restaurant/hotel") — 商店 simply combines "commerce" with "premises" into the generic word for any retail shop.

examples.hanzi: 我想去商店买一些牛奶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù shāngdiàn mǎi yìxiē niúnǎi.
examples.english: I want to go to the store to buy some milk.

examples.hanzi: 这条街上有很多小商店。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo jiē shang yǒu hěn duō xiǎo shāngdiàn.
examples.english: There are many small shops on this street.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 女 marks women and female roles, as in 妈, 姐, 妹.
支 (zhī) — near sound — 妓 is jì; 支 also sounds out 技 jì and 枝 zhī.
女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.

example.hanzi: 这部电影描写了一个妓女的悲惨生活。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng miáoxiě le yí gè jìnǚ de bēicǎn shēnghuó.
example.english: This film depicts the tragic life of a prostitute.
example.fact: 妓 pairs 女 ("woman") with 支, which pictures a hand holding a branch and by extension "a trade, a skill" — together suggesting a woman working in an entertainment trade, the historical sense from which the character's narrower modern meaning developed.

examples.hanzi: 这位作家写过一本关于妓女的小说。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zuòjiā xiě guo yì běn guānyú jìnǚ de xiǎoshuō.
examples.english: This writer wrote a novel about prostitutes.

examples.hanzi: 那部老电影讲的是一个妓女的命运。
examples.pinyin: Nà bù lǎo diànyǐng jiǎng de shì yí ge jìnǚ de mìngyùn.
examples.english: That old film is about the fate of a prostitute.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
斤 (axe) — 斤 is an axe, as in 新, 析; 断 is to cut through, shown by the axe and threads cut.

example.hanzi: 他不断地练习,直到学会为止。
example.pinyin: Tā bùduàn de liànxí, zhídào xuéhuì wéizhǐ.
example.english: He practiced continuously until he learned it.
example.fact: 断 alone means "to break, to sever" (as in 打断, "to interrupt," literally "to hit-break"), so 不断 literally reads "not broken" — describing an action or process as unbroken and continuous, the same negated-verb logic behind 不停 ("non-stop," literally "not stopping").

examples.hanzi: 雨不断地下了三天。
examples.pinyin: Yǔ búduàn de xià le sān tiān.
examples.english: It rained continuously for three days.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要不断学习新知识。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào búduàn xuéxí xīn zhīshi.
examples.english: We need to keep learning new knowledge.

components.note: 能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".
里 (village, unit) — the bottom; the dictionary takes it as the 'unit/measure' part, as in 重量 weight, 能量. 里 is also a Chinese mile.
旦 (dàn, dawn) — the top. A loose sound clue only today: liáng/liàng vs dàn. Do not rely on it.

example.hanzi: 运动可以释放身体里多余的能量。
example.pinyin: Yùndòng kěyǐ shìfàng shēntǐ lǐ duōyú de néngliàng.
example.english: Exercise can release the excess energy in the body.
example.fact: 能量 is a modern scientific coinage combining 能 ("ability, to be able") with 量 ("quantity, amount") into a literal "quantity of ability [to do work]" — a fairly transparent, compositional rendering of the physics concept "energy" built from two everyday characters rather than borrowed by sound.

examples.hanzi: 早上吃饭能给我们一天的能量。
examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang chīfàn néng gěi wǒmen yì tiān de néngliàng.
examples.english: Eating in the morning gives us energy for the day.

examples.hanzi: 太阳能是一种干净的能量。
examples.pinyin: Tàiyángnéng shì yì zhǒng gānjìng de néngliàng.
examples.english: Solar power is a kind of clean energy.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 灬 is fire at the bottom, as in 热, 照, 点; 熟 is cooked food, then ripe and familiar.
孰 (shú) — same sound — 熟 is shú, like 孰.
心 (heart) — 心 marks thought, as in 想, 思, 念; 悉 is knowing completely, as in 熟悉.
釆 (distinguish) — 釆 is distinguishing details (also in 番, 采), so 悉 is to know something thoroughly.

example.hanzi: 我对这座城市非常熟悉。
example.pinyin: Wǒ duì zhè zuò chéngshì fēicháng shúxī.
example.english: I'm very familiar with this city.
example.fact: 熟 alone already describes food that's fully cooked (成熟, "ripe, mature," shares the same root) — its extended sense "familiar, practiced" treats knowledge as something "cooked through," the same metaphor English uses when calling a skilled person "well-seasoned."

examples.hanzi: 我对这条路很熟悉,闭着眼睛也能走。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì zhè tiáo lù hěn shúxī, bì zhe yǎnjing yě néng zǒu.
examples.english: I know this road well enough to walk it with my eyes closed.

examples.hanzi: 她还不熟悉新公司的工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā hái bù shúxī xīn gōngsī de gōngzuò.
examples.english: She isn't yet familiar with the work at the new company.

components.note: 角 (horn) — an ox's horn; with 刀 (knife) the picture is cutting up an ox, so "to take apart", then to loosen and explain.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 分, 切, 到; a blade separates the parts.

example.hanzi: 我不理解这个词的意思。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bù lǐjiě zhège cí de yìsi.
example.english: I don't understand the meaning of this word.
example.fact: 解 grew from taking apart to solving and understanding: 解决 (to solve), 解释 (to explain), 了解 (to know about), 理解 (to comprehend). It is xiè in the surname 解 (Xiè).

examples.hanzi: 请你解释一下这个词。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ jiěshì yíxià zhège cí.
examples.english: Please explain this word.

examples.hanzi: 他解开了绳子上的结。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiěkāi le shéngzi shang de jié.
examples.english: He untied the knot in the rope.

components.note: 牙 (tooth) — a picture of interlocking teeth; 牙 also sounds out 芽 yá and 讶 yà.

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān shuā liǎng cì yá.
example.english: I brush my teeth twice a day.
example.fact: 牙 is the everyday word for tooth: 刷牙 (brush teeth), 牙医 (dentist), 拔牙 (pull a tooth). The formal word is 牙齿, and 象牙 is ivory (literally elephant tooth).

examples.hanzi: 他的牙很整齐。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yá hěn zhěngqí.
examples.english: His teeth are very even.

examples.hanzi: 我的牙有点疼，要去看牙医。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de yá yǒudiǎn téng, yào qù kàn yáyī.
examples.english: My tooth hurts a bit and I need to see a dentist.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.

example.hanzi: 这个故事讲的是一位公主的冒险。
example.pinyin: Zhège gùshi jiǎng de shì yí wèi gōngzhǔ de màoxiǎn.
example.english: This story is about a princess's adventure.
example.fact: 公主's title is traditionally said to trace back to a Han-dynasty custom in which a duke (公) formally stood in as marriage sponsor for an emperor's daughter, since the emperor's own rank was considered too exalted for the role — hence "the one presented by a duke." Historians debate the details, but the 公 in the title is widely linked to this practice.

examples.hanzi: 小女孩梦想自己是一位公主。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo nǚhái mèngxiǎng zìjǐ shì yí wèi gōngzhǔ.
examples.english: The little girl dreams of being a princess.

examples.hanzi: 这位公主住在一座高高的城堡里。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi gōngzhǔ zhù zài yí zuò gāogāo de chéngbǎo lǐ.
examples.english: This princess lives in a tall castle.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, as in 教, 放, 收; 效 is to imitate or produce results.
交 (jiāo) — near sound — 效 is xiào; 交 also sounds out 校 xiào and 较 jiào.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng fāngfǎ fēicháng yǒuxiào.
example.english: This method is very effective.
example.fact: 有效 literally combines 有 ("to have") with 效 ("effect, result") into "having effect" — the same 效 root appears in 效果 ("effect, result") and 有效期 ("period of validity"), the phrase commonly printed on medicine and food packaging as an expiration date.

examples.hanzi: 这张票三天内有效。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng piào sān tiān nèi yǒuxiào.
examples.english: This ticket is valid for three days.

examples.hanzi: 医生说这种药对感冒很有效。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō zhè zhǒng yào duì gǎnmào hěn yǒuxiào.
examples.english: The doctor says this medicine is effective for colds.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — traditionally 羊 over 大: a big, fat sheep was good, tasty and pleasing, hence beautiful. 羊 also appears in 样 and 洋.
今 (jīn) — the top part hints the sound — 金 is jīn, like 今; 金 means gold and metal.
金 (metal) — as a radical it shrinks to 钅 in simplified characters — 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 银 silver.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu yào yìbǎi měijīn.
example.english: This piece of clothing costs one hundred US dollars.
example.fact: 美金 literally reads "American gold" — 金 here doesn't mean the metal but is a long-standing shorthand for "currency, money" (also seen in 现金, "cash") — distinct from the more official 美元, which uses 元, the standard word for a basic currency unit shared with 日元 ("yen") and 欧元 ("euro").

examples.hanzi: 这本书在美国要十美金。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū zài Měiguó yào shí měijīn.
examples.english: This book costs ten US dollars in America.

examples.hanzi: 我想把一千美金换成人民币。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ yì qiān měijīn huàn chéng rénmínbì.
examples.english: I'd like to exchange a thousand US dollars into RMB.

components.note: 门 (gate; traditional 門) — marks doors and gateways, as in 开 open, 关 close, 间 room; 闹 has a market 市 inside a gate: a noisy, lively place, as in 热闹 bustling.

example.pinyin: Wàimiàn tài nào le, wǒ shuì bu zháo.
example.english: It's too noisy outside, I can't sleep.
example.fact: 闹 is noisy, but 热闹 (rènao) is "lively" in a good way, since noise is a sign of a happy festival or gathering. It also appears in 闹钟 (alarm clock), 闹笑话 (to make a fool of oneself) and 闹肚子 (to have an upset stomach).

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在院子里玩得很热闹。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài yuànzi lǐ wán de hěn rènao.
examples.english: The kids are playing lively in the yard.

examples.hanzi: 别闹了，我们要认真学习。
examples.pinyin: Bié nào le, wǒmen yào rènzhēn xuéxí.
examples.english: Stop messing around; we need to study seriously.

components.note: 氵 (water) — slippery as wet surfaces; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
骨 (gǔ) is only a loose sound clue; 猾 huá shares it and sounds exactly like 滑.

example.pinyin: Dìshang hěn huá, xiǎoxīn diǎn.
example.english: The floor is slippery, be careful.
example.fact: 滑 describes slippery or smooth surfaces and the action of sliding: 滑雪 (skiing), 滑冰 (skating), 滑板 (skateboard), 光滑 (smooth). 滑稽 (huájī) means comical.

examples.hanzi: 冰上很滑，别摔倒。
examples.pinyin: Bīng shang hěn huá, bié shuāidǎo.
examples.english: The ice is slippery; don't fall.

examples.hanzi: 他滑雪滑得很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā huáxuě huá de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He skis very well.

components.note: 夕 (evening) — 夕 is evening or dusk, as in 外, 多, 梦; 夜 is night.
亦 (yì) — near sound — 夜 is yè; 夜 also sounds out 液 yè.
日 (sun) — time and day, as in 早 early, 时 time, 明 bright; 晚 is when the sun is late.
免 (miǎn) is a close sound clue for wǎn; it also sounds out 勉 miǎn and 挽 wǎn.

example.pinyin: Yèwǎn de chéngshì fēicháng ānjìng.
example.english: The city is very quiet at night.
example.fact: 夜晚 doubles up two characters that both independently mean roughly "night, evening" — 夜 (built from 夕, "dusk," plus a person moving under cover of darkness) and 晚 (the sun "escaping," 免, out of sight) — reinforcing one meaning into a single, slightly more literary word for "nighttime."

examples.hanzi: 夜晚的星星特别亮。
examples.pinyin: Yèwǎn de xīngxing tèbié liàng.
examples.english: The stars are especially bright at night.

examples.hanzi: 夏天的夜晚,我们常常在院子里乘凉。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān de yèwǎn, wǒmen chángcháng zài yuànzi lǐ chéngliáng.
examples.english: On summer nights, we often cool off in the yard.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤: clear water.
青 (qīng) gives the exact sound; also 请 qǐng, 情 qíng, 晴 qíng and 精 jīng.
酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks: 酒, 醉 drunk, 酸 sour; 醒 is sobering up, then waking.
星 (xīng) sounds exactly like 醒 (tone differs).

example.hanzi: 喝了咖啡后,他感觉更清醒了。
example.pinyin: Hē le kāfēi hòu, tā gǎnjué gèng qīngxǐng le.
example.english: After drinking coffee, he felt more clear-headed.
example.fact: 醒 (built from 酉, "wine jar") originally described sobering up from drink before broadening into the general sense "to wake up" — so 清醒 literally combines "clear" with "sobered-up," letting the word cover both waking from literal sleep and having a clear, alert mind more generally.

examples.hanzi: 早上洗个冷水脸,头脑就清醒了。
examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang xǐ ge lěngshuǐ liǎn, tóunǎo jiù qīngxǐng le.
examples.english: After washing your face with cold water in the morning, your head clears up.

examples.hanzi: 他喝了酒,现在还不太清醒。
examples.pinyin: Tā hē le jiǔ, xiànzài hái bú tài qīngxǐng.
examples.english: He drank alcohol and is still not quite sober.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.
亡 (wáng) is a close sound clue for wàng; it also sounds out 忘 wàng (forget) and 网 wǎng.
月 (moon) — to gaze up at the moon, so to look into the distance, then to hope.

example.pinyin: Bié zhǐwàng tā huì lái bāngmáng.
example.english: Don't count on him coming to help.
example.fact: 指望 most often shows up in negative warnings (别指望, 不能指望) telling someone not to rely on an uncertain outcome — a more colloquial, slightly resigned register than the neutral 希望 or 期望.

examples.hanzi: 别指望他会帮你,他很忙。
examples.pinyin: Bié zhǐwàng tā huì bāng nǐ, tā hěn máng.
examples.english: Don't count on him to help you, he's busy.

examples.hanzi: 我们全家都指望这份工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen quán jiā dōu zhǐwàng zhè fèn gōngzuò.
examples.english: My whole family is counting on this job.

meanings: have a guess! (playful, reduplicated form of 猜)

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 犭 is the animal radical (犬), as in 猫, 狗, 狼; 猜 once meant a suspicious, wary animal.
青 (qīng) — near sound — 猜 is cāi; 青 also sounds out 清, 请, 情 and 晴.
犭 (animal) — 犭 is the animal radical (犬), as in 猫, 狗, 狼; 猜 once meant a suspicious, wary animal.
青 (qīng) — near sound — 猜 is cāi; 青 also sounds out 清, 请, 情 and 晴.

example.pinyin: Nǐ cāicai zhè shì shénme lǐwù.
example.english: Guess what this gift is.
example.fact: Reduplicating a one-syllable verb (猜 → 猜猜) softens a request into a playful invitation, the same pattern as 看看 ("take a look") and 想想 ("think it over") — the second syllable typically loses its tone in speech.

examples.hanzi: 你猜猜我今天遇到了谁。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ cāicai wǒ jīntiān yùdào le shéi.
examples.english: Guess who I ran into today.

examples.hanzi: 让我猜猜,你是不是想吃火锅?
examples.pinyin: Ràng wǒ cāicai, nǐ shì bu shì xiǎng chī huǒguō?
examples.english: Let me guess, do you want to eat hot pot?
